chunks: Specifying charge pump capacitors. The question: How do you spec a capacitor for a charge pump.
To specify charge pump capacitors, work backwards from how much droop and ripple you can accept.
The flying capacitor sets the pump's output resistance, so it needs enough capacitance and a low internal resistance (ESR). The output capacitor sets the ripple.
Ceramic capacitors lose capacitance when a steady voltage sits across them, so you must use the value they really have at that voltage, and give each part a safe voltage rating.
Imagine a bucket that gets smaller the fuller it is. A 1 microfarads ceramic capacitor can behave like that: with 3.
3 volts across it, it may hold only about half its labeled value. If you size your circuit using the label, you will be short on capacity.
So you always check what the bucket really holds at your working voltage. The analogy fits ceramics, but not electrolytics, which behave differently.
R out is within about 10% of the switch limit once C fly at least about 0. 5 microfarads and climbs quickly below 0. 25 microfarads.
Because of DC-bias loss, a capacitor that is 1 microfarads nominal and 0. 4 microfarads effective sits in the steep part.
Lower frequency moves the knee to larger C ( C proportional to 1 over f ).
Flying capacitor: the capacitor that moves charge from input to output ("How a charge pump works"). Output capacitor: the capacitor that holds the output steady between pulses.
Slow-switching resistance ( R SSL ): the part of the output resistance caused by the flying capacitor's limited size, 1 over (fC fly) .
DC-bias derating: the loss of ceramic capacitance when voltage is applied. Effective capacitance: the real capacitance at the working voltage and temperature.
Take a doubler at 500 kilohertz with a 1 microfarads flying capacitor. Then R SSL equals 1 over (500 000 times 10 to the -6) equals 2 ohms.
If bias derating halves the capacitance, R SSL rises to 4 ohms. For the output, a 20 milliamps load with a 10 microfarads capacitor gives a ripple of about 0.
02 over (2 times 500 000 times 10 times 10 to the -6) equals 2 millivolts. That is the whole idea.
"Flying cap from the slow-switching resistance 1 over (fC) : pick it so that's no more than the switch-limited resistance, about 1 microfarads at 500 kilohertz.
Output cap from ripple I over (2fC) plus ESR. Then spec effective capacitance after DC-bias derating, voltage rating 1.
5x or more, low ESR, and RMS current: 2I out in the flying cap. Place close to the pins."
